core.title: Decode the nominal user/system flow and its keep/pivot/kill sibling user/system flows
core.given: Product capabilities and DESIRED OUTCOMES for a main job have been kept.
core.when: The planner decodes the journey that realizes that main job.
core.then: Define the nominal user/system flow (the happy-path journey realizing the main job) and, alongside it, decide each error, alternate and exception sibling user/system flow with an explicit operator keep, pivot or kill.
prefer: Decode the nominal user/system flow first, then enumerate error, alternate and exception siblings against it.
Record the keep/pivot/kill decision for every sibling user/system flow next to the nominal user/system flow.
avoid: Decoding user/system flows before product capabilities and DESIRED OUTCOMES have been kept.
Planning only the happy path and leaving error/alternate/exception journeys undecided.
Adding sibling user/system flows without an operator keep/pivot/kill decision.
core.why: The nominal and sibling user/system flows are what a journey composes across flow routers; decoding them after capabilities/DESIRED_OUTCOMES are kept, with explicit keep/pivot/kill on siblings, makes non-happy-path scope a deliberate decision rather than an omission.
evidence: The plan names a nominal user/system flow that realizes the main job via the kept capabilities/DESIRED_OUTCOMES.
Each error, alternate and exception sibling user/system flow in the plan carries an operator keep, pivot or kill decision.
verification: Fires only during planning/decomposition, after product capabilities and DESIRED OUTCOMES have passed keep/pivot/kill; that phase state needs a new observer, so a realization must add one or judge it from the plan content.

Compliance is judged from plan content (llm_judged), not from file kinds or paths: the check asks whether the plan names a nominal user/system flow realizing the main job via the kept capabilities/DESIRED_OUTCOMES, and whether each error, alternate and exception sibling user/system flow carries an explicit operator keep, pivot or kill decision.

Terms of the check: nominal_user_system_flow is the happy-path journey realizing the main job; sibling_user_system_flows are the error, alternate and exception journeys decided by keep/pivot/kill alongside the nominal user/system flow.

values: kept capabilities/DESIRED_OUTCOMES without a decoded nominal user/system flow
nominal user/system flow without sibling user/system flows decided

fires: Planner has kept product capabilities and DESIRED OUTCOMES and now authors the user-system-flow/journey for the main job.
A plan defines the happy-path user/system flow but has not decided error, alternate or exception sibling user/system flows.
doesNotFire: Product capabilities and DESIRED OUTCOMES are still being proposed or have not yet passed keep/pivot/kill.
Coder implementing an already-planned acceptance with no plan or journey authoring.

classification.note: Neutral as-is; product capabilities and DESIRED OUTCOMES are cross-stack ATDD plan artifacts, not stack or path names.
The single obligation carried verbatim; it defines the nominal and sibling user/system flows inline, so no definition is lost.
Rationale names only ATDD planner concepts (journeys across flow routers); neutral.
Neutral ordering guidance at plan level.
Neutral recording guidance; 'next to the nominal user/system flow' is placement inside the plan, not a stack path.
Neutral ordering prohibition, mirrors the given/activation gate.

The term nominal_user_system_flow and its definition are stack-neutral planning vocabulary of this rule, not realization machinery; the term and its definition are carried in the core's verification terms.

The term sibling_user_system_flows and its definition are stack-neutral planning vocabulary of this rule, not realization machinery; the term and its definition are carried in the core's verification terms.

neutralityNotes: The whole convention is planner-methodology, so the core carries it almost verbatim: product capabilities, DESIRED OUTCOMES, user/system flows, journeys, flow routers and keep/pivot/kill are cross-stack ATDD planning concepts (the closed vocabulary itself ships capability/desired-outcome/user-system-flow/journey artifact types and URN shapes), not stack, runtime, framework, language, suffix or path names. The verifier terms nominal_user_system_flow and sibling_user_system_flows and their definitions are likewise neutral planning vocabulary and stay in the core's verification (audit r2). Nothing is Bun-specific enough for bunOnly; the per-fact observer notes' load-bearing part survives as the facts' observability values plus the core's first verification entry. The single thing the core needs from a profile is which concrete kinds play the plan-artifact role (roles.plan_artifact.kinds); no proposed key was needed.
